methodological_rigor.justification: The study combines single-cell IMC (82 high-risk NMIBC samples, 29 markers, 530,728 segmented cells, Steinbock/Mesmer segmentation, Louvain clustering, compartment-aware II/TT/IT indices with Laplace smoothing on logit scale) with an IMC-specific gated-attention MIL deep-learning model. Compartment-aware indices directly address the known pitfall of raw cell counts in multiplex imaging. Multivariable Cox models adjusted for clinical covariates, FDR correction, Hodges-Lehmann estimates with 95% CIs, and univariable/multivariable decomposition are methodologically sound. Weaknesses include TMA sampling rather than whole-slide (authors acknowledge heterogeneity concern), n=82 with 28 progression and 42 recurrence events limiting multivariable power, no external cohort, no bootstrap-corrected internal validation, and a deep-learning test set of only n=10 patients on which perfect rank separation yields inflated AUC=1.00. Statistical methods are appropriate and transparently described with explicit acknowledgment of exploratory nature.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective multicenter cohort (4 Dutch hospitals plus Stavanger) using specimens from a previously published transcriptomic series (de Jong et al.), mapping to Oxford 2b. Findings are clinically actionable if validated: CD38+ plasma cell enrichment and fibroblast:tumor ratio as markers of BCG failure could identify candidates for early cystectomy or immune checkpoint blockade. The identification of CD14/CD11b/CD68/CD8/FOXP3 as key predictive markers aligns with known biology and supports translational pathways (daratumumab, checkpoint blockade). Authors appropriately defer clinical use pending validation.

reporting_quality.justification: The study reports cohort flow (427 to 88 to 82 for single-cell; 69 to 59/10 for GA-MIL), inclusion/exclusion rationale, multicenter source, EAU-based endpoint definitions, antibody panel with exclusions, software versions (Steinbock v0.16.3, R v4.5.1, imcRtools v1.14.0, PyTorch v2.5.0), and explicit train/test separation at patient level. Effect sizes with 95% CIs, FDR adjustment, and exploratory framing are consistent with REMARK principles for biomarker reporting. Data or code availability statements are not evident in the text; no repository is cited. Test-set predictions (Table S2) and attention maps (Figure 8) add transparency.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides the first single-cell spatial IMC validation of the BRS1-3 molecular subtypes in high-risk NMIBC, confirming a BRS3-like immunosuppressive phenotype at single-cell resolution. The IMC-specific gated-attention MIL architecture extending to 18 marker channels is a meaningful technical contribution beyond prior H&E-based MIL (Fuster et al., AUC 0.68). Identification of CD38+ plasma cells as an independent progression predictor (HR 2.28) provides a novel, actionable biomarker. The compartment-aware II/TT/IT indexing is adapted from recent spatial literature (refs 31, 35) but applied appropriately here.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well structured with coherent integration of two complementary analytical strategies (single-cell IMC and GA-MIL) and clear presentation of methods, results, and limitations. Figures and tables are systematically referenced. The Discussion contextualizes findings within prior BCG and CAF literature and explicitly reframes interaction and CN/SC analyses as exploratory after FDR correction. Minor issues: the relationship between the two analytical pipelines could be more tightly integrated, and the inflated AUC=1.00 on a 10-patient test set is reported with appropriate caveats but could be more prominently qualified.

key_strengths: Single-cell spatial IMC validation of BRS1-3 transcriptomic subtypes at 530,728-cell resolution in a 82-patient high-risk NMIBC cohort
CD38+ plasma cells independently predict progression (HR 2.28, 95% CI 1.37-3.79, FDR=0.004) after multivariable adjustment and FDR correction
Compartment-aware II/TT/IT indexing with Laplace smoothing appropriate for variable-cellularity TMA data
IMC-specific gated-attention MIL model provides complementary patient-level prediction with channel-sensitivity analysis highlighting biologically coherent markers (CD14, CD11b, CD68, CD8, FOXP3)
Transparent framing of findings as exploratory with appropriate FDR correction and explicit acknowledgment of sample-size limitations
key_concerns: GA-MIL test cohort of only 10 patients yields ROC-AUC=1.00 with complete rank separation, which is statistically fragile despite Clopper-Pearson CI 0.86-1.00
TMA-based analysis may miss intratumoral heterogeneity; no whole-slide validation
Orthogonal IHC or multiplex IF validation of key cell populations (fibroblasts, CD38+ plasma cells) not performed
No external IMC validation cohort; no bootstrap-corrected internal validation of Cox models
No data or code availability statement visible; FFPE samples had ~1 year storage at -80C which may have affected staining consistency
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically strong spatial proteomics study with biologically coherent findings and complementary deep-learning analysis; the main limitation is the fragile n=10 GA-MIL test set and absence of external validation, supporting Tier 2 acceptance with minor revisions.
